title: Ulysses S. Grant — The Life, The Rise, And The Legacy #Shorts
description:
Those who met Ulysses S. Grant at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. Grant (born Hiram Ulysses Grant; April 27, 1822 – July 23, 1885) was the 18th president of the United States, serving from 1869 to 1877, and was the Commanding General of the Union Army. Grant was born in Ohio and graduated from the United States Military Academy in 1843.

The whole life of Ulysses S. Grant reads like a single decision repeated. When the discovery of gold in California brought prospectors and settlers to the territory, Grant and the 4th infantry were ordered to reinforce the small garrison there. Grant was charged with bringing the soldiers and a few hundred civilians from New York City to Panama, overland to the Pacific and then north to California.
